text:
Carla: Heads-up — control plane error rate spiked at 15:06 UTC, correlated with the v2026.3.2 rollout to canaries. I'm recommending we hold the remaining rollout slots until we confirm stability.

deploy-bot: Deploy hold placed on release v2026.3.2 by @Carla. All pending deploy slots for this release are paused. Reason: incident-triggered.

David: confirmed seeing the 502s in eu-west. Traces show increased latencies on cp-service leader election path.

Alice: copying logs, will add a short blameless note to the release thread. Any preference on pinning the previous version for autopross?

Carla: yes pin to v2026.3.1 for now. We need to avoid automatic rollups to the new variant until we have a mitigation.

Bob: ops-oncall can you validate capacity on the control plane? might be related to recent kernel patch on the pool.

ops-oncall: looking now — one control-plane leader node OOM'd and restarted. Investigating memory regression from last night's image.

Emma: product note — pause means we should update the release notes draft and delay the marketing send by 6h. I'll coordinate.

David: quick rollback option: we can cut traffic to v2026.3.1 in the router and drain canaries. That avoids rolling back DB migrations if any. Thoughts?

Carla: agree. Let's avoid DB churn. Plan: 1) keep hold 2) pin customers to v2026.3.1 3) roll back canaries via router traffic-shift 4) validate for 30m before lifting.

Alice: I'll open a tiny changelog update and annotate the release with "hold - investigating control plane 5xx". Linking: https://internal/release/v2026.3.2/notes

deploy-bot: Planned action recorded: hold + pin applied. To lift hold run: `/deploybot lift v2026.3.2 --after 30m --note "stability validated"`

ops-oncall: memory regression suspected from image digest sha256:abc123. Rolling a hotfix candidate to the control-plane leaders now (non-disruptive). Will report back in ~10m.

Bob: if hotfix looks good we can re-run canary on a small cohort and watch error rate. If it stays <0.1% for 30m, proceed staged rollout.

Emma: noted — I'll delay marketing and set a customer comms hold.

David: one more thing — we should add a short postmortem task to the release notes to avoid re-running this during next window.

Carla: agreed. For reschedule: proposing new change window at 18:00 UTC tentatively, will confirm after hotfix validation.

Alice: scheduling note added to the calendar and release checklist.

ops-oncall: hotfix deployed to leaders, initial metrics look good — error rate down to baseline. Continuing validation.

Carla: thanks. keep this thread updated. If metrics stay stable for 30m we lift the hold and proceed with the staggered rollout; otherwise we'll keep the pin and open a rollback card. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Hold status: ACTIVE. Pin: v2026.3.1. Last update by ops-oncall at 1767001258.

Bob: cheers — monitoring dashboards in the canary lane: https://dashboards/internal/canary/v2026.3.2

Carla: (no objections) standby for lift or rollback decision.

ops-oncall: validation complete — 45m stable after hotfix. Recommend lift.

Carla: lifting hold in 2m and running a small canary sweep. Deploybot, please execute the staged resume.

deploy-bot: Acknowledged. Executing staged resume for v2026.3.2: step1 -> 2% traffic, step2 -> 10% after 10m, step3 -> 50% after 20m, final -> full after 40m unless rollback triggered. Operator: @Carla.

Alice: updating release notes to mark incident and mitigation. Will include rollback rationale and the pin lifecycle.

Emma: I'll re-open marketing schedule and update stakeholders.

Carla: closing the hold thread once rollout completes successfully. Great job team.
